summary: Oil heir Charles Koch ran Koch Industries while it hid deadly benzene, mercury and pipeline hazards, and spent decades funding libertarian think tanks, university institutes, dark money groups and the Tea Party to dismantle US regulation.

evidence.note: story opens with Fred Koch's refining process and patent fight with big oil in the 1920s
Fred Koch's firm builds a major refinery in Hamburg for the Nazi-era fuel drive
Nazi-sympathizing nanny and Fred's beatings of the boys described at length
Fred dies in 1967 and the sons inherit the company; Charles takes control
Charles funds LeFevre's Freedom School from 1966
worker Donald Carlson not told of abnormal benzene blood tests, dies of leukemia
Corpus Christi refinery underreports benzene emissions, company indicted in 2000
corroded Koch pipeline leaks gas and explodes, killing two teenagers in Texas
David Koch runs as Libertarian vice-presidential candidate in 1980
1996 Triad Management dark money attack ads and Senate investigation
Mercatus Center at George Mason and influence over academic research
2016 election, Koch network's clash with Trump, up to 2018 tweets
